**Answer: 16**

**Upper bound.** Take any colour class $S$. Every square of $S$ has at least two neighbours (horizontal or vertical) in $S$. Consider the subgraph of the grid induced by $S$. It has minimum degree at least 2, so it contains a cycle. Every cycle in the grid graph has length at least 4, so $|S| \ge 4$. (Equivalently, a set of 3 or fewer squares cannot give every square two same-coloured neighbours: a path of 3 has endpoints with only one neighbour.) With 64 squares and each colour used at least 4 times, there are at most $64/4 = 16$ colours.

**Construction.** Split the board into sixteen disjoint $2\times 2$ blocks and give each block its own colour. In a $2\times 2$ block, each square is horizontally and vertically adjacent to exactly two other squares of that block, and both have the same colour. So every square has at least two same-coloured neighbours, and 16 colours are achieved.

ANSWER: 16
